# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — Host 10.11.26.183

**Capture:** 2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap
**Capture window:** 2024-11-26 04:49:38 UTC – 05:43:18 UTC (54 min)
**LAN:** 10.11.26.0/24

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** (Dell/Intel NIC — vendor prefix `d0:57:7b`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NetBIOS name service, confirmed) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES (domain controller NEMOTODE-DC / NEMOTODES-DC, 10.11.26.3, realm `nemotoads.health`) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **oboomwald** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString`, client-side ticket requests from 10.11.26.183) |

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client, trojanized/repurposed as a remote-access trojan.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The bundled Suricata/ET alert log fires the following on this host's traffic to 194.180.191.64:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (65 hits)
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (2 hits)
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is independently corroborated at the packet level: every C2 POST carries `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and a body of `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` (client heartbeat) alternating with `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<binary>` (encrypted command/response payload) — the documented NetSupport client wire protocol, not a generic HTTP fetch.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
| Indicator | Detail |
|---|---|
| **C2 endpoint** | **194.180.191.64:443** — POSTs to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (plaintext HTTP carried over port 443, not TLS) |
| Beacon pattern | First checkin 04:50:45 UTC, then steady ~60-second interval POSTs continuing to the end of the capture (05:43 UTC) — classic NetSupport heartbeat |
| GeoIP lookup domain | `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 / 104.26.0.231 / 172.67.68.212 (Cloudflare) — client queried `GET /location/loca.asp`, server returned coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877` |

### Malicious/suspicious domain (likely initial lure)
| Domain | Resolved IP | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **modandcrackedapk.com** | 193.42.38.139 | Queried via DNS at 04:50:14 UTC, then a TLS ClientHello with SNI `modandcrackedapk.com` to 193.42.38.139:443 at 04:50:40 UTC. Flagged by `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `...in TLS SNI`. The name (modded/cracked APK site) and ET category are consistent with a cracked-software/fake-download lure — the likely delivery path for the NetSupport client, occurring roughly 5 seconds before the first NetSupport C2 checkin. This session is TLS-encrypted in the capture, so the dropper itself could not be recovered or hashed from this evidence.

### Transferred files / hashes
No malicious binary was transferred in cleartext HTTP in this capture — all HTTP-visible objects are benign OS/software update or connectivity-check artifacts (Windows CTL updates, MS NCSI test, Adobe ARM check, OCSP/CRL lookups). I extracted and hashed every HTTP object in the pcap; none correspond to an executable or archive payload. The likely payload delivery (from `modandcrackedapk.com`) rode inside TLS and cannot be hashed from this evidence — **no payload SHA256 can be substantiated from this capture.**

### Noted but not attributed to compromise
- Concurrent DNS/TLS activity to `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) and `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) around 04:50:11–04:50:15 UTC — timing places these alongside the modandcrackedapk.com session (ad-redirect/subscription-lure chain), but no C2-style beaconing or malware signature is associated with them; included for completeness, not asserted as C2.
- Several GPL/ET NETBIOS SMB alerts (SMBv1 use, "NTLMSSP overflow attempt", IPC$ access, MS-EFSR request) between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3). Packet sizes and content are consistent with routine legacy SMBv1/AD authentication traffic rather than an active exploitation or lateral-movement attempt — flagged by IDS but not corroborated as malicious activity in the packet contents.

## Summary

10.11.26.183 (DESKTOP-B8TQK49, user **oboomwald**) contacted **modandcrackedapk.com** (193.42.38.139) at 04:50:40 UTC, and within 5 seconds began beaconing to **194.180.191.64:443** using the **NetSupport RAT** client protocol (`User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, `/fakeurl.htm` POLL/ENCD checkins), sustaining ~60-second beacons for the remainder of the capture. Attribution to NetSupport RAT is signature-confirmed by ET/ETPRO rules and corroborated by the raw protocol content. No cleartext dropper or payload hash could be recovered — delivery is presumed to have occurred over the TLS session to the lure domain, which is not decryptable from this evidence.
